subject: Request: SLA responsibility rebalance for OxyClone private gateway
messages:
From: Alan Jenkins <alan.jenkins@oxyclone-med.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Li <rachel.li@oxyclone-med.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@oxyclone-med.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private gateway — SLA responsibility rebalance request

David — thanks for taking a look. We're preparing to move production traffic to our private on-prem edge gateway next month and need to align the SLA language around availability and network latency attribution. High level: the gateway (managed by OxyClone network ops) terminates customer traffic before it hits Redwood Private; we can provide telemetry but cannot control the transit peering or the customer WAN.

Specific asks: 
- Exclude gateway-to-origin latency (our edge) from Redwood latency SLOs when we present evidence of an incident (router logs, traceroutes).
- Add a fallback routing expectation (best-effort) rather than a guaranteed failover timeline for cross-datacenter peering.
- Insert an operational evidence protocol (what logs and timestamps count) so we don't get SLA credits for issues outside Redwood's serving surface.

I've attached a network diagram and a draft appendix that shows where we believe responsibility should sit. We're under procurement review and need a written position from Redwood legal/ops for our security team.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of next steps.

— Alan
Head of Infrastructure, OxyClone Medical
attachments: oxyclone_network_diagram.pdf (diagram), proposed_sla_appendix.docx (draft appendix)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Jenkins <alan.jenkins@oxyclone-med.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private gateway — SLA responsibility rebalance request

Alan — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Quick read-through notes: the diagram helps; the draft appendix is a good starting point. We understand the need to avoid false positives on SLA claims when the customer-controlled edge is at fault.

Next steps from our side:
- I'll loop in Ops and Legal to validate scope of exclusions and evidence types.
- Can you confirm the minimum set of telemetry you can supply in real-time (syslog, BGP state, traceroutes, timestamps) and retention window? That determines whether the exclusion can be automated or requires manual adjudication.
- We'll propose specific language that keeps Redwood's uptime SLOs meaningful while acknowledging the handoff boundary.

Kimberly — tagging you for legal guidance on wording around "best-effort" failover versus an objective failover SLA. Vanessa — ops: please advise on what evidence footprint we need to accept a customer-origin latency exclusion.

I'll follow up with a proposed appendix by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Alan Jenkins <alan.jenkins@oxyclone-med.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private gateway — SLA responsibility rebalance request

Alan / team — appreciate the appendix. A few legal/contract principles to keep in mind: 
1) We can include an "attributionable cause" carveout where, given acceptable evidence, Redwood will not issue SLA credits for incidents attributable to customer-controlled network elements. The key is defining acceptable evidence and timelines for submission.
2) We should avoid language that implies Redwood provides an operational failover guarantee for a third-party-managed gateway. "Best-effort" is reasonable, but let's be explicit: we can offer documented runbooks and can recommend configuration patterns that improve failover probability, but cannot guarantee specific RTO for customer-managed peering.
3) For auditability, require signed post-incident evidence (log bundles with UTC timestamps + sha256) within a 30-day window to be considered for attribution. If evidence is incomplete, incidents will default to the standard SLA determination process.

Proposed additions to appendix (will draft precise clause): 
- Evidence types allowed: router syslog, traceroute outputs with timestamps, BGP session logs, NAT translations where applicable.
- Evidence submission and verification timeline: 30 days to submit, 10 days for Redwood to verify.
- Exclusion only applies when customer evidence demonstrates the primary degrading event occurred upstream of the Redwood serving boundary.

Connor — ops, how feasible is verification within 10 business days for complex multi-hop incidents?

Best,
Kimberly
Head of Legal, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alan Jenkins <alan.jenkins@oxyclone-med.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private gateway — SLA responsibility rebalance request

Alan — quick ops note from our verification perspective: 
- We can accept the evidence types Kimberly listed. For automation, we need structured traces (pcap or structured syslog) and a minimal attribution timeline. Freeform traceroute text is OK for initial triage but won't support automatic exclusion.
- Verification cadence: for incidents where the customer supplies full logs as defined, we can complete verification in 5 business days (not 10). For partial evidence we'll escalate to manual adjudication which can take up to 30 days.
- Recommendation: add a short "evidence quality matrix" to the appendix that maps evidence completeness to expected verification timelines so both sides have clarity.

We can work with your network ops to agree sample telemetry exports and a one-time onboarding checklist to avoid friction later. If procurement needs an initial legal position now, Kimberly's language above is a good start; we'll iterate on the matrix.

— Vanessa
Mgr, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
